unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)

unit_note: Improvised army-level group commanded by Generaloberst Kurt Student, formed from 1 April 1945 on the left wing of Army Group H (OB Nordwest from about 6 April) with II Parachute Corps, part of LXXXVIII Corps and the Wehrmachtbefehlshaber Niederlande (FMS B-414, Geyer, R814, German pp. 22-23 and Anlage 2, claim C9453; FMS B-674, Geyer, 'Gruppe Student formed 1.4'). LXXXVIII Corps came under it from 3 April and returned to the Twenty-Fifth Army on 6 April (FMS B-762, Prittwitz, R810, German pp. 2 and 4; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, R668, p. 550, 'Army Group Student'). On 6 April Student's staff was given the Weser defence and on 10 April Blumentritt and Student exchanged commands (B-414): the staff continues as Army Blumentritt (GER-ARMY-BLUMT; lineage UL026, 6 April 1945). Not in the Lexikon. Added 14 November 2026 (roadmap 351; Scott approved the task). Review (leftovers-1115, task c, roadmap 351, 15 November 2026, approved by Scott, t419u): unit_note old value: "kept as a separate record, no lineage row, see roadmap 351"; new value: lineage UL026; reason: FMS B-283 (Blumentritt, R845) p. 103: on the order of Busch he took over "Armee Student" as "Armee Blumentritt"; B-414 (R814): Student's staff was given the Weser defence on 6 April. Command relations: CR1314 now ends on 1945-04-06 and CR1316 (II Parachute Corps) between 1945-04-02 and 1945-04-10.

Western Front service in April 1945 only (Thuringia, Weser and Harz); the Lexikon page also covers its earlier Eastern Front history; the staff was rebuilt in April 1945 under Hitzfeld and then Lucht and was captured near Blankenburg on 23 April.

Formal national command of the Dutch Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (Netherlands Forces of the Interior; also Nederlandse Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten, NBS), entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 14 November 2026 on branch small-fixes-1113. NIMH, De oprichting van de Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (R1163, opened 14 November 2026): on 31 August 1944 SHAEF, at Queen Wilhelmina's wish and on Prince Bernhard's urging, authorised the formation of the BS; Prince Bernhard became its commander-in-chief, under Eisenhower; on 5 September 1944 (Dolle Dinsdag) the BS was established by Royal Decree, uniting the LKP, RVV and OD. The same page records that the BS was a temporary organisation, to be dissolved three months after the German capitulation, and that it was dissolved on 8 August 1945. A second family, the Dutch Wikipedia article Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (R1164, opened 14 November 2026), also dates the official founding to 5 September 1944 and names Prince Bernhard as commander; it gives the dissolution only as August 1945. The veterans' site binnenlandsestrijdkrachten.nl (opened 14 November 2026, not given its own reference id) cites Koninklijk Besluit Staatsblad E62 of 5 September 1944 and Bernhard's appointment as Bevelhebber der Nederlandse Strijdkrachten on 3 September, and places his headquarters first in London, later in Brussels, and in November 1944 at Breda (staff in a tax office; himself at landgoed Anneville). Those headquarters statements are not used as location claims: they describe the Bevelhebber's staff, are dated only as November for Breda, and London is not a place already in the dataset. NIMH's statement that Bernhard was under Eisenhower is not entered as a command relation to SHAEF (ALL-SHAEF-000H): a second independent family opened for this pass (Dutch Wikipedia; the veterans' site) does not name SHAEF or Eisenhower as the BS's superior, and the 16 May 1944 civil-affairs agreement on liberated territory is not by itself an assignment of this formation. parent_unit_id is left blank. The Stoottroepen and Bewakingstroepen are recorded as organic components from the 22 September 1944 split south of the great rivers (de Jong, deel 10a, pp. 561-563, R894; NIMH R1163 also names the Stoottroepen as the armed branch of the BS). Lodders and Kraandijk, Militaire Spectator 1994 (R1162): Limburg, by its relationship with the Americans, took increasing distance from Commando Zuid; the three Limburg battalions came under the Koninklijke landmacht section of Prince Bernhard's staff on 2 January 1945 and transferred into the KL in January; Brabant companies were employed by the British from 11 October 1944 and transferred into the KL in May, at which point Commando Zuid was abolished. Those transfers are noted and are not given invented end-days. No new numbered Allied parent is entered for the regional commands. Review (branch small-fixes-1113, 14 November 2026, approved by Scott): old value none, new value this unit. record_status is placeholder (old value would have been active): the unit has no claim file, because no opened source names a place for the 5 September 1944 Royal Decree, and a location claim is not invented. UK-DIST-NETH is the same pattern (a sourced higher command without a location row). The formed date and the command relations stand.

Formal territorial command of the Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten in Noord-Holland north of the IJ (gewest 11), entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 12 November 2026. De Jong, deel 10b, p. 706: around Dolle Dinsdag (5 September 1944) the lieutenant-colonel of infantry (KNIL, retired) J. G. M. Wastenecker, then gewestelijk commandant of the OD, unified the armed resistance in the district; he later appears as commandant of the BS in Noord-Holland Noord (p. 1315). Colonel Koot's orders came through well in this gewest (de Jong citing van Ojen). It published the only BS-gewest narrative in book form (De mannen van overste Wastenecker, 1947). Independent (no parent in the table; the overall BS command under Prince Bernhard and Colonel Koot is not a unit). formed_date 5 September 1944 is "omstreeks Dolle Dinsdag", when de Jong first describes Wastenecker as the district commander (then still of the OD); by April 1945 the same command is the BS gewest. The gewestelijke Stormtroepen of about 200 men (mostly former KP, p. 706) are not entered as a separate unit. Added in the de Jong 10a-1 follow-up 2 (dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026).

Formal guard and rear-area units of the Dutch Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten, entered under Scott's irregular-forces rule (HANDOFF standing rule 21) after his approval of 12 November 2026. De Jong, Het Koninkrijk, deel 10a, pp. 561-563: on 22 September 1944 van Houten split the BS south of the great rivers into Stoottroepen (to fight with the Allies) and Bewakingstroepen (guard duties behind the front and of the camps) and gave command of the Bewakingstroepen to W. Regional command of the Stoottroepen in Noord-Brabant. De Jong later names de Groot commandant of the Brabantse Stoottroepen; he was dismissed and sent to London some time after the beginning of January 1945, after which the Brabant battalions were likewise converted to light infantry (p. 760). G. H. Bensen is named as acting commander in Noord-Brabant around 1 January (p. 760) but no appointment date is given. Organic parent NL-INF-STOOT. formed_date is the first documented company, not a separately dated charter of the regional command. unit_name: Task Force A (1st Tank Destroyer Brigade)
unit_note: Provisional task force of the Third Army formed for the Brittany north shore railway under Brigadier General Herbert L. Earnest, headquarters the 1st Tank Destroyer Brigade, with the 6th Tank Destroyer Group, 15th Cavalry Group and 159th Engineer Battalion, about 3,500 men (Blumenson, Breakout and Pursuit, ch. 21). Under VIII Corps; soon dissolved after the fall of Brest (ch. 30). The id uses the headquarters, the 1st Tank Destroyer Brigade. Brigades Batch 2.

Provisional mechanised task force of VI Corps under Brigadier General Frederick B. Butler, the deputy corps commander; official designation Provisional Armored Group, VI Corps (Clarke and Smith, ch. 5, n. 6). Brigade-sized: 117th Cavalry Reconnaissance Squadron, 753rd Tank Battalion (two medium companies), 2nd Battalion 143rd Infantry, a company of the 636th Tank Destroyer Battalion, 59th Armored Field Artillery Battalion. Dissolved as a separate entity by the 36th Division on 23 August 1944 but used again as a task force until the end of the Montélimar battle; Butler returned to VI Corps afterwards (ch. 10). Brigades Batch 2.
